issue.mint_text: mint letter below the eagle's thunderbolt not readable in the photos

new.story: A big bronze ten centimes from the France of Napoleon the Third, dated 1867 — three years before his empire collapsed in the Franco-Prussian War. One side carries the Emperor's head wreathed in laurel, ringed by his name and title; the other shows the imperial eagle standing on a thunderbolt, the emblem Napoleon's regiments had carried into battle, with EMPIRE FRANCAIS above and DIX CENTIMES below between two stars. These heavy bronze pieces were the workhorse small change of France for decades — struck in the tens of millions, they stayed in pockets and tills into the next century, which is why so many survive as worn as this one.
new.notes: Both sides photographed in the holder. Identification rests on the owner's own reads from the coin in hand, confirmed against the catalog: obverse NAPOLEON III EMPEREUR around the laureate head with the date 1867 below the portrait; reverse the imperial eagle on a thunderbolt, EMPIRE FRANCAIS above, DIX CENTIMES at the bottom flanked by two stars (a star separator is visible in the photo at the right of the reverse legend). The coin is heavily worn and dark, and the photos alone defeated letter-by-letter transcription on the first pass — the catalog match (the laureate-head bronze 10 centimes struck 1861-1868 is the only French issue combining this portrait legend, eagle reverse and bottom value) plus the owner's reads carry the identification. The mint letter below the thunderbolt is not readable in the photos, so no mint is claimed. Condition, per the owner: the coin is clipped and has a hole through the center - the dark center mark visible in both photos is the hole, not a plug. Value revised down accordingly: holed and clipped, it sits in the bulk/cull range.

source: photo NOID_France_1867_10Centimes_obv.jpeg (pen label: FRANCE 1867 10 CENTIMES); legends and year read by the owner from the coin and matched to the catalog, 2026-11-09
